close_reason: Resolved as part of PKIX-hy2e.22. LintParameter now has both #[non_exhaustive] and a LintParameter::new(id, label, default_value) constructor.
description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:381:

    pub struct LintParameter {
        pub id: Cow<'static, str>,
        pub label: Cow<'static, str>,
        pub default_value: Cow<'static, str>,
    }

This struct is the in-memory form of an OSCAL Catalog `parameter`. The
doc itself (lines 366-376) lists OSCAL parameter fields that are
'not modelled here': constraint, guideline, select, link.

Three of those (constraint, guideline, select) cover constraint
validation rules that the workspace's parameter mechanism doesn't
support today. The OSCAL Profile composition (resolve_profile in
oscal/profile.rs) doesn't enforce them either — it just emits the
parameters and trusts Lint::set_parameter to validate.

When the workspace eventually decides to expose constraint/select
slots (e.g., to let an OSCAL Catalog say 'max-octets MUST be between
1 and 32' without each Lint impl duplicating that range check), every
new field is a breaking change because LintParameter is not
#[non_exhaustive].

Combined with the lack of a constructor:

    let p = LintParameter {
        id: Cow::Borrowed(\"max-octets\"),
        label: Cow::Borrowed(\"Max octets\"),
        default_value: Cow::Borrowed(\"20\"),
    };

every lint that ships a parameter uses struct-literal construction.
The day `constraint: Option<...>` is added, every lint's parameter
constructor needs an update.

# Cheapest fix

Add #[non_exhaustive] and provide:

    impl LintParameter {
        pub fn new(
            id: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>,
            label: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>,
            default_value: impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>,
        ) -> Self { ... }
    }

Then `LintParameter::new(\"max-octets\", \"Max octets\", \"20\")` becomes
the construction path, and the struct itself is evolvable. The
shipped Rfc5280MaxSerialLengthLint and any future parametric lints
get the constructor for free.

# Combined with PKIX-hy2e.22

This is one of the structs called out in PKIX-hy2e.22 (the sweeping
#[non_exhaustive] finding). Filing separately because LintParameter
is a particularly clear case — the OSCAL spec literally has the
extension slots already, and the rustdoc admits the limitation. Same
fix shape but its own visibility.
title: API contract: LintParameter has no constructor and no #[non_exhaustive], OSCAL parameter shape locked
